$comment: Streak parity table (ARCHITECTURE §4.13): S1 to S13 of PRD §4.4.8; AC-RPR-01 to 04 and 09, AC-STK-08 and 09, AC-FRZ-01 to 05 and AC-INC-03; and our own rows: an evaluation run twice (one freeze spent), a pending date across midnight, an on-time finish over a stored Freeze (refunded) and over Protected, a westward hop that can't reopen a served date, a hop with and without 20 hours since the previous call, a second date-line protection inside 30 days, and two repairable archive finishes back to back (one repair).
Replayed by Vitest against the engine (src/engine/streaks/streaks-fixture.test.ts) and, from SQL-6, by the generated SQL parity tests against private.evaluate_streak and private.apply_finish.

credit: decisions memo §14.1, which replaces AC-STK-09's 20-hour rule. A Daily for local date D is accepted only for D in [utc_today - 1, utc_today + 1]; it earns streak credit only when D is later than the last credited (Played or Repaired) date; a run whose device zone changed since the previous Daily is kept out of the crowd's numbers (zoneChanged, honest-play flag 16) but still earns credit.
finish: applyFinish on its own: the counters before, the finish (kind and the gap status already stored for its date), the counters after and the status written.

scenarios: a stored start state, then requests in order. A read is a get_streak call; a finish is the streak hook of a finished attempt (on_time: a ranked attempt inside its window; unranked: archive, a challenge of that date, or a resumed abandoned attempt). Both compute the effective today from the request's zone and the latest date served (maxServed), and a finish evaluates first, with an on-time attempt's own date held pending. A finish's kind is on_time when its date is later than the last credited date, repair when an unranked play's date is repairable at that moment, else other. The figures after a finish (after) are a summary that decides nothing. lastFinish (zone and offset) is stored by every finish, lastRepairAt by a repair, datelineUsedAt by a read or finish that protects a date by the date-line rule.

start.days expands { from, to, status } ranges (to defaults to from). Missing start fields take the empty ledger's values. Instants are UTC; Europe/London is UTC+0 in November 2026, America/Los_Angeles UTC-8, America/New_York UTC-5, Australia/Sydney UTC+11, Pacific/Auckland UTC+13, Pacific/Kiritimati UTC+14, Asia/Tokyo UTC+9 and Etc/GMT+12 UTC-12.

expect compares only the fields it names. days names stored statuses after the step (null: no status). A repair offer is { date, dailyNumber, until } with DAILY_EPOCH = epoch, and until is local 00:00 on the date + 3 in the request's zone. display is active, paused (exactly when a repair is offered) or broken (a Missed date in the history, no offer, and the current streak below the best, so record-first copy leads until the new run reaches the record).

Choices this table pins down where the PRD leaves room: the date-line candidate is the first gap date the walk decides after the latest Played or Repaired date (an incident that protects it uses the rule up); a request that decides a stored candidate starts no new one; the cooldown needs more than 30 days since the last date-line protection; a date protected by the date-line rule writes no notice (the only protected copy names an outage of ours), and an incident's protected notice is written only while a streak is alive; an undecided date (a pending attempt's or a candidate) links the chain without counting; the stored best never goes down; breakTooLong holds only while the break's last date would still be inside a one-date repair window.

credit.title: a first Daily for the server's UTC date is accepted and earns credit
D = utc_today + 1 (an early morning at UTC+14) is accepted
D = utc_today - 1 (an evening at UTC-12) is accepted
D = utc_today + 2 is refused, so it earns nothing
D = utc_today - 2 is refused, so it earns nothing
D equal to the last credited date is accepted but earns no credit
D before the last credited date can't backfill a missed day, whatever the device says
a zone change since the previous Daily keeps the run out of the crowd's numbers but still earns credit
an eastward zone change is flagged the same way and earns credit

finish.title: an on-time finish stores Played and counts toward the next freeze
the 7th counted finish grants a freeze and resets the progress
the 14th counted finish grants the second freeze
with 2 held a finish grants nothing and progress stays at 0
an on-time finish over a stored Freeze plays the date and refunds the freeze
a refund that fills the second slot leaves progress at 0, so that finish grants nothing more
with 2 held, the refund over a stored Freeze is lost to the cap
an on-time finish over Protected plays the date and refunds nothing
an on-time finish over a Missed date (an open attempt's date that was decided anyway) plays it
a repair turns Missed into Repaired and counts toward freezes
an archive play of a Freeze date changes nothing and refunds nothing
a repair of a date with no stored status changes nothing
other (no credit, or a second repair inside 168 hours) changes nothing

scenarios.title: played D-3 to D-1, plays D: streak 4
played to D-1, nothing on D, read on D+1 with 1 freeze: D Freeze, freezes 0, streak unchanged
played to D-1, nothing on D, read on D+1: D Missed, current 0, displayed Paused at the old count, repair until the end of D+2
S3, then on D+1 plays D+1 and repairs D: streak old + 2
played to D-1, nothing on D or D+1, read on D+2: two Missed dates, no repair, streak 0, Broken
played to D-1, nothing on D to D+2, read on D+3 with 2 freezes: D and D+1 Freeze, D+2 Missed and repairable until the end of D+4
S3 with a repair used 5 days ago: Broken until the 168 hours pass inside the window (D+1 played meanwhile), then Paused with an offer
S7 when the cap opens only after the window closes: the break stays final and the new run shows record first
played to D-1, a 15-minute heartbeat gap on D, no play on D, 1 freeze: D Protected, freeze kept, streak unchanged
starts D at 23:58 local and finishes at 00:04 on D+1: D Played, and D+1 is still today
finishes D in Los Angeles, opens the app in Sydney about 20 hours later on D+2, then plays D+2: D+1 undecided, then Protected by the date-line rule
in London plays D-1, opens at D+1 00:30 (D Missed), then a request from UTC-12 (local D): today stays D+1 and D can only be repaired
two eastward jumps of 12 hours or more, 10 days apart, each followed by a second request in the new zone: only the first gap date is Protected
played to D-1 in London; one request from UTC+14 at D+1 08:00 UTC, then back in London: nothing Protected, D Missed and repairable
a jump that lasts one request protects nothing, and its candidate then takes a held freeze like any gap date
a jump of 12 hours or more with no change of zone name protects nothing
exactly 30 days after the last date-line protection the rule is still closed
a second later than 30 days the rule may start a candidate again
a zone hop 17 hours after the previous call still earns streak credit (memo §14.1: no 20-hour rule)
the same hop 20 hours after the previous call earns credit the same way
an on-time finish for a date not later than the last credited date earns nothing, so a zone change can't backfill a Missed day
a 10-day streak to D-1, no play on D; on D+1 finishes D+1, then D from the archive: streak 12
the same repair at 23:59 on D+2, after D+1 and D+2 were finished on time: streak 13
the same play at 00:00:01 on D+3 is an unranked archive play and the streak stays broken
a second repair within 7 x 24 hours of the first is refused, and the cap names when the next one opens
a break of two consecutive uncovered dates offers no repair for either date
while a repair is possible every figure shows the pre-break 23 as paused, never 0; after the repair: 23 + 1 + today = 25
the 7th, 14th and 21st finished Dailies grant a freeze until 2 are held; with 2 held the 21st grants nothing and progress shows 0 of 7
one missed date with 1 freeze held: the freeze is spent, the count is unchanged and a freeze notice waits for the next visit
two missed dates with 2 freezes: both are spent and the streak survives
three missed dates with 2 freezes: the first two are covered, the third breaks the streak and is offered for repair
with no live streak a missed date spends no freeze (a held freeze, and a chain already broken by a stored Missed date)
a protected date spends no freeze
a 12-minute heartbeat gap on the player's local date D (11-11 in UTC, 11-10 in New York), no play on D: streak and freezes intact
an evaluation run twice in the same moment spends one freeze and writes one notice
a date whose ranked attempt stays open across midnight is undecided until its window closes, then Missed, and resuming it repairs
the same open attempt with a freeze held: once its window closes the freeze covers the date and the chain stays whole
an on-time finish over a stored Freeze plays the date and refunds the freeze
an on-time finish over a stored Protected date plays it and refunds nothing
a westward hop can't reopen a served date: after UTC+14 served D+1, London's local D stays an archive date
two repairable archive finishes back to back repair once: the second finds the 168-hour cap closed
an incident after the streak broke still protects its date, but writes no notice that the streak is safe
when an incident already protects the first gap date, the date-line rule isn't used and the next gap date is ordinary
a player with no finish yet has nothing to walk
